findings.title: S3 bucket policy does not enforce TLS (SecureTransport)
findings.description: Without an explicit Deny on aws:SecureTransport=false, bucket objects can be fetched over plaintext HTTP. Add a bucket policy statement denying s3:* when SecureTransport is false.
findings.expected: bucket policy denying s3:* when SecureTransport is false
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace wildcard (`*`) actions and resources with the minimum scoped ARNs the workload needs. Split policy authoring from attachment. Use IAM Access Analyzer to generate scoped policies from CloudTrail history.

findings.title: S3 bucket without lifecycle configuration
findings.description: Hygiene: S3 buckets should define lifecycle rules to transition or expire objects, controlling long-term storage costs. Add a lifecycle_rule block or an aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration resource.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: S3 bucket encrypted with AWS-managed key, no customer-managed key
findings.description: This bucket encrypts objects with an AWS-managed key (SSE-S3 AES256, or SSE-KMS with the AWS-managed aws/s3 key) instead of a customer-managed KMS key. A CMK gives you key rotation control, grants, CloudTrail audit of key use, and the ability to disable or delete the key. Set kms_master_key_id to a customer-managed key. Unencrypted buckets are AEGIS-AWS-001's job and are not reported here.
findings.expected: kms_master_key_id set to a customer-managed KMS key
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.

findings.title: Cloud SQL instance with public IP
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance with settings.ip_configuration.ipv4_enabled = true exposes the database to the internet. Use private IP with VPC peering instead.
findings.remediation: Remove public exposure. Restrict ingress to known CIDR ranges, disable public IPs / public access, and use Private Service Connect / VPC Service Controls if external access is required. Verify with `gcloud compute firewall-rules list`.

findings.title: Cloud SQL instance without SSL enforcement
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance with settings.ip_configuration.require_ssl = false accepts plaintext database connections.
findings.remediation: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Set `min_tls_version = "TLS_1_2"` / `minimum_tls_version`, replace HTTP with HTTPS, and redirect HTTP→HTTPS.

findings.title: Cloud SQL instance without deletion protection
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance with deletion_protection = false (the provider default) can be destroyed accidentally. Enable deletion protection for production databases.
findings.remediation: Enable deletion protection to prevent accidental destruction. For Cloud SQL and Compute instances set `deletion_protection = true`. For GCS buckets there is no deletion_protection argument — instead remove `force_destroy = true` (or omit it; the default is false) and consider a `retention_policy` or a resource-manager lien for critical data.

findings.title: Cloud SQL instance without maintenance window
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance with no maintenance_window lets GCP apply disruptive maintenance at any time; hygiene finding.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Cloud SQL instance without IAM database authentication
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance without database flag cloudsql.iam_authentication=on forces password-only auth.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace broad roles with the minimum predefined or custom IAM roles the workload needs. Use Workload Identity Federation and service accounts with minimal scopes.

findings.title: Cloud SQL instance without log_disconnections
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance without database flag log_disconnections=on misses session audit data; hygiene finding.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity + Data Access), VPC flow logs, and Security Command Center. Ship logs to a dedicated project with locked retention.

findings.title: Cloud SQL instance not highly available
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance with settings.availability_type other than REGIONAL (the default is ZONAL) has no standby in another zone: a zonal outage takes the database offline. Use availability_type = "REGIONAL" for production.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against Google Cloud security best practices and the CIS Google Cloud Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.description: google_sql_database_instance with no settings.password_validation_policy block accepts weak database passwords (short, no complexity requirements). Enforce a password validation policy.
findings.remediation: Apply least privilege. Replace broad roles with the minimum predefined or custom IAM roles the workload needs. Use Workload Identity Federation and service accounts with minimal scopes.

findings.title: Cloud SQL MySQL instance without binary logging
findings.description: google_sql_database_instance with a backup_configuration block but binary_log_enabled not true keeps no binary logs: MySQL point-in-time recovery and change auditing are impossible. Enable binary logging.
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on Cloud Audit Logs (Admin Activity + Data Access), VPC flow logs, and Security Command Center. Ship logs to a dedicated project with locked retention.
